transcript.text: A repeating beep is most often the fridge-freezer’s door or high-temperature alarm, rather than an immediate component failure. Check that both doors shut squarely, nothing is caught on a shelf or drawer, and the rubber seals are clean and sitting flat all the way round. Also consider whether warm shopping has just been loaded or a door has been open for a while; it can take several hours to settle. Are both the fridge and freezer still properly cold, and do both doors close fully without food, drawers or packaging stopping them?
fridge is cold, freezer seems to be running. the bottom freezer drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night, a bag was sticking out

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The bag holding the drawer out is the most likely reason for the beeping: warm air will have entered and triggered the freezer door/high-temperature alarm. Remove anything that can foul the drawer, push it fully home and make sure the seal sits flat all round, then keep the freezer shut as much as possible for a few hours. It may continue to beep until the temperature has recovered; if there is an alarm-reset button, it may silence the sound but the freezer still needs time to cool. If it keeps alarming once the drawer is most likely closed and the food is still properly frozen, the remaining possibility is that the drawer or seal is not closing squarely.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok pushed it in, still beeping. freezer number is flashing -9 and theres a red alarm symbol. what do I do about the beep?

To silence it, press the button marked Alarm, a bell symbol, or a crossed-out bell once; on some controls it needs holding for about 3 seconds. Keep the drawer shut and avoid opening it unnecessarily while it cools. If there is no alarm/bell button, send the make and model or a clear photo of the control panel, as the reset control varies.
found a button with a bell on it, pressed it and the beep stopped. should I leave it now?

Yes — leave it shut now and let it recover. Avoid opening it unless necessary for the next several hours, and make sure bags cannot stop the drawer closing fully again. Once it gets back towards -18°C, the display and alarm should settle; if it is still flashing or not properly frozen after about 24 hours, it would need further checking.
